# the contributor audit: general convex-body surface midpoint repair


disintegration dependency. This is not an OC proof or a numerical depth
payment. the contributor read both complete new sources:

* `candidate d7f1891e34b3ec5a`;
* `candidate f38040720425d155`.

The new ball argument also has optimal-midpoint's independent full audit
of Sections 3--7, and rate-geometry independently checked its geometric
and differentiation steps.

## 1. Exact ordinary background verified

the contributor inspected the actual Caravenna--Daneri preprint, Section 3.1,
Definitions 3.1--3.2, Theorem 3.3, and Remark 3.4. The theorem disintegrates
Lebesgue measure restricted to an arbitrary finite-measure Borel set
over the convex function's gradient fibers, and gives both directions
of absolute continuity with the appropriate face Hausdorff measure
restricted to that set. The zero-dimensional fiber case is included.
The preprint is available at
[the authors' paper](https://cvgmt.sns.it/media/doc/paper/1434/disFacceConvCD.pdf).

The graph-surface transfer in the new source does not use the
dimensionally imprecise sentence in the paper's Remark 3.5. It applies
the area formula with H^(d-1), multiplies by a Jacobian constant on each
gradient fiber, and then uses the constant intrinsic Jacobian of the
affine graph lift on that fiber. This is the correct normalization.

Local patches alone would not prove equivalence on the whole exposed
face. The new source supplies the missing argument: if a chart has
positive conditional mass, equivalence activates every chart with a
relative-open overlap in that face. Connectedness of its relative
interior propagates this to the complete face. Countability removes
only one normal-marginal null set. This proves full support, relative
boundary nullity, and equivalence globally, without a smooth normal
stratification or continuous conditional-density assertion.

## 2. Ball localization and dimension alignment

At a regular point on the cutting sphere, uniqueness of the truncated
body's normal would make the point c+r n. The strict inequality
h_K(n)<n.c+r rules this out. Thus on that open normal set, ball truncation
retains exactly the original surface measure in the open ball. A point
of the exposed face in that ball ensures both the strict inequality and
full dimensionality of the truncated body.

For each rational pair of balls, the established surface-area
power-mean inequality and actual contact domination give a conditional
ball inequality on the contact normal set. The common normal reference
measure is preserved. Taking a countable union of exceptional sets,
then approximating arbitrary balls from inside, gives the inequality
for all ball centers on one full-measure set of normals. No center is
chosen first and then assigned its own exceptional null set.

The dimension proof correctly differentiates the target Radon measure
with respect to a homothetically pushed input conditional measure. Its
positive lower ratio forces that pushed input to be absolutely continuous
with respect to the target. Equivalence with face Hausdorff measures
then bounds the target face dimension by each input dimension. Actual
Minkowski face inclusion supplies the reverse bounds and alignment of
their direction spaces. This avoids assuming target density bounds at
possibly exceptional midpoint points.

## 3. Every good endpoint pair, one selected transport

The target upper-ball-density representative agrees almost everywhere
with the actual conditional density and may be infinite on a null set.
The input differentiation sets have full marginal measure. Since the
ball inequality holds for every center simultaneously, it yields the
weighted density envelope for EVERY pair in those sets. This is stronger
than an almost-everywhere product-pair assertion, which would not suffice
for singular optimal couplings.

The inverse endpoint maps first prove absolute continuity of the output
law. The weighted area formula and common positive matrix identity then
give domination by the target upper-density representative. Its exceptional
null set already carries no output mass. Hence the domination is by the
actual target conditional surface measure. Compact finite-test separation
selects one coupling above the prescribed old law in all convex tests.

The separately audited Borel assembly theorem integrates these choices
and the rebuilding martingales over arbitrary normal measures. It retains
the prescribed physical endpoint crossflows, source and target measures,
and existing cap allocations. Literal closed-cap midpoint implications
remain valid for the one selected tuple law. The d=1 endpoint case is
direct and uses counting measure.

## 4. Scope

The preceding polytopal restriction is removed for the three-fiber
boundary midpoint repair. Neither this generalization nor the new
conditional density inequality turns convex order into source-halfspace
order. The exact square obstruction remains valid. No parity-wide source
mass allocation, OC center, or factor gamma_d follows automatically.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
